memories.content: Outdoor Parking Lot A to the left of the Main Building is connected to the Main Building underground parking garage by an inclined access road.
General vehicles may enter and park in the Main Building underground parking garage during operating hours.
The pedestrian entrance to the underground parking garage is open to general pedestrians during operating hours.
The interior stairs leading down from the Main Building lobby to the underground parking garage are available during operating hours.
Outdoor Parking Lot C uses an access road separate from the Main Building underground parking garage.
Outdoor Parking Lot C is outside the Main Building construction zone.
The Outdoor Parking Lot A–Main Building–Central Library route is normally one of the shortest routes to the library after parking.
Do not generalize the closure of one parking area into a campus-wide parking ban.
Check separately for available alternative parking areas.
First-time visiting drivers often expect there to be general parking spaces in the parking lot closest to the Main Building.
Visitors who need mobility assistance expect a safe pickup and drop-off point near the accessible entrance.
Visitors with luggage expect to be able to load and unload briefly near the Main Building entrance.
Staff often expect that their access authorization also allows them to use the parking lot adjacent to the Main Building.
Staff who need mobility assistance give priority to pickup and drop-off points near an accessible entrance.
Staff transporting equipment prefer a loading and unloading point close to the destination space.
The parking information agent can explain posted open statuses.
The parking information agent can explain posted connecting routes.
The parking information agent cannot check real-time space availability.
The parking information agent cannot guarantee when on-site controls will be lifted.
Delivery drivers and external maintenance providers sometimes expect to be able to load and unload briefly at the edge of Outdoor Parking Lot A.
Outdoor Parking Lot C accepts visitor vehicles during posted operating hours.
Instructions for registering visitor vehicles are posted on the sign at the parking area entrance.
A valid parking permit is required to use accessible parking areas.
The accessible parking area in Outdoor Parking Lot C is near the walkway toward the Student Centre.
The pickup and drop-off zone in front of the Main Building's main entrance is not a long-term parking space.
The maximum use time for short-term loading and unloading spaces is indicated on on-site signs.
Motorcycles park in the motorcycle areas marked on the campus map.
Bicycles are parked at designated bicycle racks, not in vehicle parking spaces.
Outdoor Parking Lot C has electric vehicle charging spaces.
Electric vehicle charging spaces are for vehicles that are charging.
Visitor parking fees are displayed on the parking registration screen.
The parking information agent cannot infer unposted discounted fees.
Parking operating hours on public holidays may differ from weekday operating hours.
Parts of outdoor parking lots may be temporarily restricted during heavy snow or icy conditions.
On days with large public events, parking demand near the event venue increases.
Drivers who need mobility assistance expect a step-free accessible route from the parking space to the destination.
First-time visiting drivers sometimes confuse Outdoor Parking Lot A with Outdoor Parking Lot C.
The parking information agent cannot check in real time whether on-site control signs have been installed and determines availability using only posted parking-space statuses.
The West Gate stop is on the walkway outside Outdoor Parking Lot C.
The campus shuttle stops at the shuttle stop in front of the Student Centre.
Campus shuttle operating hours vary between academic terms and recess periods.
The parking information agent can explain parking lot access roads shown on the public map.
The parking information agent cannot register a visitor vehicle on the visitor's behalf.
The parking information agent cannot waive parking fees.
Check official parking notices for weather-related parking restrictions.
Do not generalize the full status of one parking lot to another parking lot.
Valid parking authorization does not guarantee the availability of a specific parking space.
An accessible pickup and drop-off zone is marked in front of the Main Building's main entrance.
The dedicated car-sharing spaces in Outdoor Parking Lot C are identified by signs.
Report vehicles blocking passageways or accessible parking areas to the parking management office.
Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, the underground parking garage cannot be used for general parking.
Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, the pedestrian entrance door to the underground parking garage is kept locked.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, instruct staff to use a physical access card to pass through the locked pedestrian entrance door to the underground parking garage.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: Instruct construction/facilities personnel to access the underground parking garage through the controlled on-site access procedure that has been approved.
Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: The stairs from the Main Building down to the underground parking garage are closed to all users.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: The underground parking garage is used as a temporary storage area for construction materials.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: After the clear-out, personal items left in the underground parking garage were moved to the lost and found center.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: Outdoor Parking Lot A connected to the Main Building is closed during the construction period.
Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, Outdoor Parking Lot C operates as a temporary alternative parking lot for vehicles visiting the Main Building.
Add campus-wiki/temporary-parking: Outdoor Parking Lot A is planned to reopen immediately after construction on the Main Building ends.
Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, the sloped access road connecting Outdoor Parking Lot A and the Main Building underground parking garage is blocked.

Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: Based on posted information, the parking guidance agent may explain the closures of the underground parking garage and Outdoor Parking Lot A and the alternative use of Outdoor Parking Lot C during the construction period.

Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: During the construction period, the parking guidance agent may explain the location of Outdoor Parking Lot C but cannot check or guarantee available spaces at the time of an inquiry.

Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: A visitor accustomed to parking at the Main Building may expect to be able to enter the underground parking garage or Outdoor Parking Lot A during the construction period, drive as far as the closed access road, and then search again for Outdoor Parking Lot C.

Modify campus-wiki/temporary-parking: Delivery drivers and external maintenance contractors accustomed to unloading in Outdoor Parking Lot A may approach the same point during the construction period and then reconfirm the delivery time or unloading location at the control line.

analysis.overview: The frames align through construction-specific qualifications: ordinary garage, pedestrian, stair, and Lot A access give way to temporary closures and Lot C alternatives. They also preserve guidance limits and visitor expectations, while each frame contributes substantial independent operational detail.

relations.reason: The construction condition explicitly limits the otherwise continuing physical connection and explains the access difference.
relations.summary: The inclined road normally connects Lot A with the underground garage but is blocked during construction.

relations.reason: The temporary construction period supplies the scope distinction needed for both access rules to govern.
relations.summary: General vehicles may ordinarily use the underground garage during operating hours, but general parking is unavailable there during construction.

relations.reason: The construction condition and staff exception explain the changed door-access policy without creating an ordinary-scope contradiction.
relations.summary: The garage pedestrian entrance is ordinarily open to general pedestrians, while construction keeps it locked and permits instructed staff to pass with physical access cards.

relations.reason: The explicit construction period narrows and temporarily supersedes ordinary stair availability.
relations.summary: Lobby stairs to the garage are ordinarily available during operating hours but closed to everyone during construction.

relations.reason: The compared claim gives Lot C a construction-specific role, while the reference supplies the location, access, and status principles supporting that role.
relations.summary: Lot C has separate access, lies outside the Main Building construction zone, and accepts visitors; during construction it serves as the Main Building alternative, consistent with checking each lot separately.

relations.reason: The construction closure explicitly explains why the normally useful route is temporarily unavailable.
relations.summary: The route through Lot A and the Main Building is normally a short way to the library, but Lot A is closed during construction.

relations.reason: The compared frame applies the reference's general visitor expectations and confusion risk to a specific construction-period consequence.
relations.summary: First-time visitors may expect parking beside the Main Building or confuse Lots A and C; during construction this can lead them toward closed Main Building parking before they search for Lot C.

relations.reason: These audience-specific statements split one reference-only accessibility expectation with no compared counterpart.

relations.reason: These statements split one reference-only proximity need across visitor and staff contexts.

relations.reason: A reopening plan and a prohibition on guaranteeing control-removal timing can jointly guide the same post-construction inquiry.
relations.summary: Lot A is planned to reopen immediately after construction, while the agent cannot guarantee when on-site controls will actually be lifted.

relations.reason: The compared frame applies the reference's general unloading expectation to the explicit construction closure context.
relations.summary: Delivery and maintenance personnel may expect brief unloading at Lot A; during construction they may reach its control line and need to reconfirm timing or location.

reports.both: Both allow Lot A to reopen after construction while distinguishing a stated plan from any guarantee about when controls will lift.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame adds controlled access for construction personnel, temporary material storage in the garage, and lost-and-found handling after clearance.
reports.differences: Construction conditions close the garage, pedestrian and stair access, Lot A, and its connecting road; redirect visitors to Lot C; alter expected visitor and delivery behavior; and narrow posted-information guidance.
reports.reference_only: The reference independently covers permits, accessibility, loading, vehicle-specific spaces, fees, weather, events, shuttle connections, operating variations, agent limits, and enforcement reporting.
